frontmatter.title: Optimization and variational methods
frontmatter.description: Checked four-qubit QAOA and two-qubit VQE examples, with complete optimization traces and separate sampled readout.

children.value: QAOA alternates an objective-dependent phase with a mixer, while VQE changes a trial state to reduce its energy

. Both are hybrid workflows: classical parameter search and repeated state preparations needed to evaluate an objective belong to the algorithm. Here we make those operations inspectable on two small problems.

The examples use explicit Qiskit circuits, exact statevector objectives, independent classical references, and separately seeded finite-shot experiments. The downloadable traces record every objective evaluation and all sampled readout. They check these particular circuits and runs; they establish no large-instance convergence guarantee or quantum advantage.

The resource record contains logical circuit inputs and the complete demonstrated workload. Arbitrary rotations remain unsynthesized. Physical qubits, surface-code runtime, fault budgets, and a physical Pareto frontier are
, pending an audited synthesis and error-budget contract.

The complete ideal toy-workflow execution took 0.594446 s on this CPU, including exact reference checks, post-fit quality checks and probability generation. Artifact drawing/export and logical-ledger compilation are outside that workflow timer.

Finite-shot results evaluate the first optimized state only. These are independent ideal multinomial samples, not executed hardware shots. The standard error is estimated from the joint measured observable; it is not a rigorous confidence interval. The Hoeffding radius separately gives an ideal-sampling 95% bound for each listed estimate, not simultaneous coverage across this table.

The first QAOA state’s exact probability of an optimal cut is 0.531249794; 7 independent ideal draws suffice for at least one optimum with probability at least 0.99 at these fixed parameters. This is a readout statement, not an optimizer guarantee.

The ledger also stores each exact evaluation’s parameters, logical gates and depth. These simulated circuit counts are separate from shot-weighted readout counts. Arbitrary rotations remain unsynthesized; physical qubits, T counts, factories and runtime are pending. Reset timing, routing, graph/input transfer, noise and mitigation are excluded. Reference checks are included in whole CPU workflow time but are not timed separately.

children.value: The primary fitted angles are then evaluated in separate ideal finite-shot experiments with seeds

. Samples are drawn classically from statevector probabilities; repeated physical circuits are not executed. These experiments do not feed sampled objectives back to the optimizer. They report counts, sampled objectives, exact expectations, sample standard errors, and achieved output quality. Changing initialization probes optimization variability; changing the sampling seed probes readout variability. Neither experiment tests device noise, error mitigation, nor convergence of a sampled optimizer.
Logical workload and the pending physical handoff

children.label: Logical workload and the pending physical handoff

children.value: accompanies actual measured OpenQASM 3 circuits. It records gate counts, depth, width, input preparation, all sampling repetitions, basis changes, and readout. The graph is a classical edge list and the Hamiltonian is three explicit Pauli terms; no data-loading oracle is assumed. Classical input parsing, physical reset and measurement time, and device routing are excluded. Reference calculations are included in the whole CPU workflow timer, but their separate time is unmeasured.

The demonstrated workload contains six exact classical optimization runs with their entire evaluation traces, plus three seeded readout experiments for each primary state. The ideal readout protocol represents 6,144 four-qubit QAOA preparations and 12,288 two-qubit VQE preparations, including both measurement bases. The generated ledger weights the explicit circuits by these shot counts; the samples themselves are drawn classically from statevector probabilities. Exact optimization evaluations use zero shots. Turning them into a hypothetical quantum optimization workload would require a stated per-evaluation measurement allocation and a new sampled optimization experiment. Multiplying one final circuit by an optimizer iteration count would not establish that workload’s convergence or accuracy.
The elementary exports retain H, CX, and one-qubit rotations. Arbitrary-angle RX, RY, and RZ gates are

synthesized into Clifford+T. The inputs support a later synthesis audit, but supply no validated T count, code distance, factory allocation, physical-qubit count, or quantum runtime. Coherent rotation approximation error and stochastic fault probability need separate budgets before a surface-code comparison. The existing
From a source checkout with the pinned Python 3.12 environment:

python scripts/generate_optimization.py
python -m pytest tests/test_optimization.py
python scripts/execute_notebooks.py

uses the same implementation as the artifact generator and provides the reusable outputs embedded above. Saved outputs serve a static website; no live Python kernel is required. To run the downloaded notebook separately, place the

The QAOA generator accepts a supplied graph and layer angles; the VQE generator exposes its ansatz parameter. Materialization is capped at 100,000 unitary gates before optional final measurements; the ledger includes those measurements. QAOA exact statevector simulation defaults to a small configured bound with a hard cap of 16 qubits; exhaustive enumeration has its own hard cap of 20. Circuit export is separate from these classical computations. Larger exports do not imply affordable simulation or project the number of optimization evaluations needed at larger sizes.
